Project overview

  • Team: Cross-regional global design initiative (UK, US, Brazil, Costa Rica)
  • Core skills demonstrated: Enterprise Informatio we n Architecture (IA), Component-Driven UI Design, B2B SaaS Workflow Optimisation, Accessibility Compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA), Design Systems

What this project proves about me: I can rapidly deconstruct bloated legacy enterprise platforms under tight sprint deadlines, translating complex workflows into scalable, modern, and accessible design frameworks without sacrificing data density.

The challenge

As part of a worldwide initiative to elevate the user experience across Equifax's B2B systems, the global design team initiated an exploratory sprint across multi-regional design hubs (Costa Rica, Brazil, the UK, and the US). The objective was to challenge legacy desktop-only paradigms and explore cohesive, future-facing interaction models.

Legacy enterprise software frequently suffers from accumulated technical and visual debt. In our existing B2B platform, internal and external corporate users grappled with three persistent issues:

  1. Inefficient Screen Real Estate: A static, top-heavy navigation header occupied significant vertical space, leaving limited viewport height for core workflows.
  2. Cognitive Overload in High-Density Views: Administrative forms and primary data tables lacked clear visual hierarchy, relying on harsh gridlines, repetitive actions per row, and fragmented error handling.
  3. Inconsistent Brand Integration: Core enterprise screens felt visually detached from Equifax's modern brand guidelines, under-utilising brand equity and subtle visual grouping techniques.

Our cohort of four regional designers was tasked with reimagining three core application templates: the primary enterprise dashboard, structured administrative forms, and the high-density data table.

Above: Baseline audit of the legacy desktop suite, illustrating the fragmented visual language, rigid navigation structures, and high interaction friction across tables and forms.

Constraints & Sprint Parameters

  • Strict 5-day delivery window: Completed while managing active business-as-usual workloads, requiring disciplined scoping.
  • Constrained direct user research: Required operating on established usability heuristics (Jakob Nielsen) and translating proven Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) ergonomics into enterprise workflows.
  • Technical feasibility: Concepts had to adhere to standard browser display capabilities and allow modular engineering implementation (e.g., responsive 12-column bento grids).

My process

  1. Heuristic Evaluation & Component Audit: Deconstructed the provided legacy wireframes and production views, isolating key failure points in navigation ergonomics, form validation, and tabular scanning.
  2. Structural Architecture & Wireframing: Formulated a modular bento grid foundation for dashboard widgets and established a dual-state collapsible sidebar to recapture vertical screen space.
  3. Concept Exploration & Brand Balance: Iterated on three dashboard directions to test varying levels of visual density, data contrast, and Equifax red brand application.
  4. Workflow Ergonomics (Forms & Tables): Redesigned multi-stage enterprise input forms and complex data tables, integrating progressive disclosure, inline expandable rows, and context-aware action bars.
  5. Design System Integration & Handoff: Structured reusable component tokens (spacing, typography, WCAG-compliant colour pairings) to facilitate regional cross-sharing and engineering appraisal.

What I did

1. Navigation Restructuring & Global Utilities

The existing navigation relied on an uncollapsible top bar that truncated content and lacked iconographic wayfinding. I overhauled this into an ergonomic, collapsible vertical navigation drawer.

  • Dual-State Mechanics: When collapsed, the sidebar preserves screen real estate by displaying tooltipped icons for experienced power users. When expanded, explicit text labels guide infrequent users, reducing cognitive recall.
  • Relocation of Global Utilities: Global utilities (Help, Documentation, Language Switcher) were extracted from the header and pinned to the navigation footer. This reinforced spatial grouping and supported F-pattern reading behaviours, keeping the primary header clear for situational context.

Above: Collapsible sidebar component states, illustrating expanded hierarchical categories, collapsed icon states, and anchored global controls.

2. Bento Grid Dashboard Exploration

To manage disparate data streams (API call volumes, licence consumption, usage schedules), I implemented an adaptable bento grid system. I explored three distinct concepts to identify the right balance between brand presence and functional clarity:

  • Concept 1 (Colour-Rich Variation): Explored enhanced colour differentiation across widget categories to test scannability for multi-metric monitoring.

Above: Concept 1 exploring distinct chromatic coding to assist visual segmentation across disparate API operational widgets.

  • Concept 2 (Minimalist & Brand-Aligned): Rationalised extraneous colour fills, utilising a controlled grey spectrum accented with the Equifax brand palette to clarify primary metrics.

Above: Concept 2 transitioning to neutral content cards with refined typographic hierarchy, directing focus to critical data visualisations.

  • Concept 3 (Strong Brand Integration): Leaned into the Equifax visual language, introducing bold header treatments and higher-contrast status cards while maintaining a clean, professional aesthetic.

Above: Concept 3 testing high-visibility brand accents, structured revenue visualisations, and dark interactive module components.

Above: Comprehensive side-by-side comparison of the three dashboard iterations submitted to the global design review cohort.

3. Detail Page & Account Settings

Applying the visual framework to deep-level administrative screens, I replaced rigid borders with subtle background contrast (#F8F9FA vs #FFFFFF) and generous card padding to demarcate operational regions.

Above: Before-and-after progression of the account settings view, showing how modern card grouping eliminates visual clutter.

4. Enterprise Form Architecture & Inline Feedback

Administrative forms were re-engineered around clear visual groupings and rigorous error prevention:

  • Input Field Styling: Standardised inputs with rounded geometries, distinct hover/active states, and accessible helper text.
  • Error States & System Status: Embedded proactive inline validation and unmistakable error summaries, removing ambiguity during complex data entry.
  • AI Assistance Integration: Conceptualised an inline AI contextual assistant widget to help administrative users navigate complex security and permission parameters.

Above: Redesigned enterprise user provisioning flow illustrating inline validation banners, structured inputs, and permission controls.

Above: Legacy user provisioning interface featuring unorganised vertical inputs and ambiguous error displays prior to redesign.

5. High-Density Data Tables

Tabular data represents the backbone of enterprise software. The legacy system suffered from visual noise caused by heavy borders, nested icons, and clumsy pagination controls.

  • Legibility Without Heavy Borders: Alternating subtle row fills (zebra striping) replaced harsh borders, preserving scan lines across wide monitors.
  • Progressive Disclosure: Expandable rows were added, allowing operators to inspect sub-level logs inline without navigating away or opening disruptive modals.
  • Floating Bulk Actions: Replaced individual row action clutter with a consolidated "more actions" menu, complemented by a persistent bulk-action bar that appears when multiple items are selected.

Above: Legacy user management table displaying redundant action icons and poorly differentiated search and filter controls.

Above: Re-engineered enterprise data table featuring consolidated pill filters, clear sort states, and expandable inline rows.

Before and After Comparison

Before: Above: The original four core templates—fragmented navigation, cluttered inputs, and poor typographic scale.

After: Above: The cohesive redesign suite—demonstrating unified typography, cohesive card mechanics, and consistent visual hierarchy.

Why I made these decisions

Above: The reimagined Equifax B2B portal interface, balancing API performance metrics, analytics visualisations, and role-based administrative controls.

  1. Adopted a Bento Grid over Fixed Multi-Column Layouts: Enterprise dashboards must serve varied roles—from security administrators to commercial directors. A modular bento grid allows engineering teams to dynamically surface or hide functional cards based on user permissions without breaking page flow.
  2. Shifted from Heavy Grid Borders to Surface Tinting: In enterprise tabular design, heavy cell borders introduce visual friction. Using alternating subtle grey tints and white backgrounds reduces visual noise and aids horizontal eye-tracking across wide screens.
  3. Relocated Secondary Utilities to the Navigation Base: B2B operators rarely access Language or Help docs multiple times per hour. Removing them from the top header declutters primary focus areas and reinforces spatial grouping conventions common in modern enterprise platforms.
  4. Implemented Inline Expandable Rows over Modals: Context switching is a primary productivity killer in enterprise data management. Allowing users to preview row-level detail inline preserves their scroll location and mental model.

Impact / results

Evaluation Area Legacy Platform State Redesigned Sprint Concept
Vertical Screen Efficiency Top navigation bar consumed ~120px of static vertical height Collapsible sidebar reclaims full vertical viewport height (100vh layout)
Data Table Scanning Cluttered per-row action buttons; high risk of misclicks Grouped context menus + floating multi-select action bar
Accessibility Compliance Low contrast text elements (<3:1); missing required-field distinction Full WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA compliance across buttons, inputs, and state tags
Cross-Regional Alignment Disjointed regional implementations across international teams Unified component baseline presented to global design leadership
  • Global Cohort Recognition: My submission was highlighted by US design leadership for its rigorous application of enterprise usability heuristics and balanced brand integration.
  • Design System Blueprint: The bento grid tokens, form patterns, and table interaction paradigms were catalogued as reference components for subsequent B2B platform development cycles.

Tools and skills applied

Roles performed on this project

  • Lead UX Architect: Audited baseline legacy usability, restructured global information architecture, and redesigned tabular interaction flows.
  • Senior Product Designer: Created component-level mockups, designed three visual dashboard directions, and standardised form and table components.
  • Sprint Contributor: Collaborated across multi-region workshops with colleagues in the US, Brazil, and Costa Rica to unify future-state design thinking.

childMarkdownRemark.html: Equifax initiated an international design sprint bringing together regional designers across the US, UK, Brazil, and Costa Rica to reimagine core legacy B2B desktop portals. Given a strict one-week timeframe and limited initial user access, I audited legacy UI patterns, defined an ergonomic collapsible navigation system, and structured a scalable bento-grid dashboard architecture. Across the week, I developed three distinct brand-aligned dashboard concepts, overhauled complex administrative input forms with inline validation, and modernised dense data tables through expandable inline rows and progressive disclosure. The resulting high-fidelity concepts delivered an accessible, WCAG-compliant design framework that balanced dense enterprise workflows with modern visual clarity, establishing a foundation for cross-regional system alignment.
